2. Contraband and Weapon Permits

Level 1 to 4 firearms and ammunition are Low-Level, Mid-Level, High-
Level and Critical-Level Contraband, respectively. Gun frames and pistol
frames share the level of the corresponding gun.
There is no permit for Level 4.

Permits placed in the Display Case attract gun buyers
(Chapter 2). The highest Weapon Permit in the store
determines the level of goods brought by many
visitors and guns requested in orders (Chapters 6, 7, 8
and 9).

2. Gun Buyers

Class I, Class II and Class III Weapon Permits in the
Display Case attract Lower Level Citizens,
Mercenaries and Upper Level Citizens buying guns,
with base chances of 50%, 40% and 35%, respectively.

There are three types of orders: custom orders, "best
in class" orders and orders to improve the stats of a
customer's own gun (Chapter 7). After a deal, the
customer may ask for ammunition (Chapter 9).

Gun buyers have three special identities: Gang Members belong to the
Black Market, Elite Mercenaries to the Lower Levels and Security Tactical
Officers to Security. They request a gun of a particular class and level,
paying its market price plus 25% (Chapter 7).
3. Gun Sellers

A Firearm Neon Sign in the Display Case has a 40%
chance of attracting a gun seller, with Lower Level
Citizens and Mercenaries in a 100 : 90 ratio. A Heavy
Firearm Neon Sign has a 25% chance of attracting an
Upper Level Citizen selling a gun. See Chapter 8 for
their guns.
During a Lower Levels Gang War, 19.4% of Lower

Level Citizen gun sellers are Gang Members, carrying only Level 2 guns.
With a Class III Weapon Permit in the Display Case, 9.4% of Mercenary
gun sellers are Elite Mercenaries and 9.4% are Security Tactical Officers,
carrying only Level 3 guns. Security Tactical Officers also require at least
30 Security reputation.
4. Buyers Attracted by Displayed Goods

Buyers attracted by weapon goods in the Display Case depend on their
total value. Below 145, a Scavenger visits, or a Self-Defense Enthusiast if
Store Attractiveness reaches 400. From 145, a Self-Defense Enthusiast
visits. From 350, starting on day 14, a Private Security Contractor visits.

Guns in a gun cabinet placed in the Display Case count as guns placed
directly in the Display Case (Chapter 10).
5. Faction Operations
Faction operations affect visitors whose business involves guns:

-<pos=7.5>Lower Levels Gang War: Gang Members appear as both gun buyers
<pos=7.5>and sellers. The chance of Thieves and Petty Thieves carrying intact
<pos=7.5>guns doubles, as does the chance of Thieves carrying Heavy rounds and
<pos=7.5>40 mm grenades.

-<pos=7.5>Station-wide Crackdown or Martial Law: Thieves and Petty Thieves
<pos=7.5>carry no intact guns, and Thieves carry no Heavy rounds or 40 mm
<pos=7.5>grenades. Faulty guns are unaffected.

-<pos=7.5>Revolution Mobilization or Increased Weapons Demand: the chance of
<pos=7.5>a Revolution visitor offering a long-term contract doubles.
1. Repair Customers

Repair customers are attracted by a repair certificate in the Display Case
(Chapter 4). Each brings 1 to 3 guns: 1 gun in 70% of visits, 2 in 20% and 3
in 10%. The next gun is presented after the current deal is completed.
Each gun's level is selected separately according to the store's current
repair certificate level (Chapter 4).

Each gun has 2 to 4 different faults. The customer mentions at least 1 of
them. At least 1 other fault is unmentioned and must be found by
inspection (Section 3).

At least 1 fault mentioned by the customer can be repaired with the
store's current supplies, including emergency repairs. Repair customers
do not visit if the store has none of the following: Screwdriver, Wire
Cutter, Plasma Cutter, Gun Parts, 3D Printing Filament, Rubbing Alcohol,
a liquid that can replace Rubbing Alcohol (Section 2), or Kotton Fabric
with durability remaining.
Two Types of Customers

On average, 1 in 3 repair customers also requests improvements after
repair and states a budget in Credits for repairs and attachments
combined. These customers bring only guns that accept attachments.
Other repair customers' guns cannot have attachments fitted.

The budget depends on gun level: Restricted I, 150 to 350 Credits;
Restricted II, 250 to 450 Credits; Restricted III and critical contraband, 400
to 700 Credits. Budgets for all guns are added together, then increased by
bonuses such as Store Attractiveness. The customer states the resulting
amount. Each completed deal deducts that gun's payment from the
budget.
2. Faults and Repairs

Surface faults are examined with a Magnifying Glass; internal faults with
a Portable XRay Scanner. Guns in the "Old and antique guns" class have
no Wiring fault. Each fault has a full repair and an emergency repair.
Emergency repairs pay less, add less promotion progress and prevent this
customer from returning (Section 6 and Chapter 4).

Rust and Fouling

Drag Rubbing Alcohol or Kotton Fabric onto
the gun. If the other item is also in the store,
this performs a full repair, using each once.
With only one item available, it performs an

emergency repair; using the other item later completes the repair. Each
use consumes 1 bottle of Rubbing Alcohol. Kotton Fabric has 1000
durability and loses 200 per use, allowing 5 uses per piece.

A liquid container can replace Rubbing Alcohol if it contains at least 25
ml of Alcohol and Alcohol makes up at least 60% of its total liquid. Each
use consumes 25 ml of liquid from the container.
3. Inspection

Drag a Magnifying Glass onto a faulty gun to perform a
surface inspection. This reveals all surface faults,
including a filed-off serial number (Section 7).

Drag a Portable XRay Scanner onto a faulty gun
to perform an internal inspection. This reveals
all internal faults.

Each type of inspection can be performed once per gun and
does not consume the tool. Guns not owned by the store can

also be examined, such as guns offered by sellers on the counter. Each
fault found on a repair customer's gun adds a row to the Gun repair
order window. The last two lines of the tooltip's "Faults" section state
whether each inspection has been performed.
4. Payment
Payment is calculated separately for each gun, in the following steps.

-<pos=7.5>Step 1, repair fee: paid once per gun according to the store's current
<pos=7.5>repair certificate level. Levels 1 to 4 pay 15, 30, 50 and 80 Credits,
<pos=7.5>respectively.

-<pos=7.5>Step 2, faults: each fault row in the window pays the amount in the
<pos=7.5>table below for its status. "repaired" pays the full repair amount,
<pos=7.5>"emergency repair" pays the emergency repair amount, and "needs
<pos=7.5>repair" pays 0. Amounts depend on gun level.

-<pos=7.5>Step 3, stolen gun: if a filed-off serial number has been found, multiply
<pos=7.5>each amount from Step 2 by 1.5 and discard the fractional part.

-<pos=7.5>Step 4, fitted parts: fitted attachments and the Gun Parts consumed by
<pos=7.5>successful refurbishment are included at their current value. This row
<pos=7.5>is labeled "Your parts on the gun".

-<pos=7.5>Step 5, bargaining: multiply each amount from Steps 1 to 4 by (100 -
<pos=7.5>discount percentage) ÷ 100, or by (100 + markup percentage) ÷ 100.
<pos=7.5>Round each result to the nearest integer.
-<pos=7.5>Step 6: add all the amounts above to obtain the total.

Example: the store has a Level 2 repair certificate and the gun is
Restricted II. Fully repair Loose or missing screws, use only Rubbing

Bargaining

Repair customers can bargain through the Bargain panel, which offers
only "Selling: Offer Discount" and "Selling: Add Markup". Bargaining
adjusts each amount as described in Step 5. Bargaining is allowed once
per customer, and the result also applies to that customer's remaining
guns. Bargaining does not affect promotion progress.

For customers requesting improvements, bargaining also changes the
budget. Offering a discount increases the budget by 2 times the discount
percentage; a 10% discount, for example, increases the budget by 20%.
Accepted markups of 10%, 25%, 50% and 75% reduce the budget by 10%,
15%, 20% and 25%, respectively.

A markup may be rejected. Payment remains unchanged if the customer
stays; the customer may also leave (Section 5).
5. Completing a Repair Order

In the trade window, "Gun repair order" lists "Level N repair fee" and the
status and payment for each known fault under "Bonus Requirements".
"Base Requirements" includes "At least one fault repaired"; customers
requesting improvements also have "Total within the budget". All base
requirements must be met to select "Accept Offer".

-<pos=7.5>Repairs cannot be undone. If the total exceeds the budget, only
<pos=7.5>attachments can be removed.

-<pos=7.5>The total is paid immediately on completion of the deal, and the gun
<pos=7.5>leaves the counter with the customer.

-<pos=7.5>If the customer leaves without a deal, either after being dismissed or
<pos=7.5>after a markup request, work ends on both the gun on the counter and

<pos=7.5>any guns not yet presented. Fitted attachments and Gun Parts
<pos=7.5>consumed by refurbishment are returned to the store. Materials
<pos=7.5>consumed by fault repairs are not returned.
Note: A customer requesting improvements may have insufficient budget to repair every fault. Check the budget before starting repairs.

Completing a repair deal increases reputation with the customer's faction
by the same amount as selling goods of equal value, calculated from the
total before bargaining. Lower Level Citizens and Mercenaries increase
Lower Levels reputation; Upper Level Citizens increase Upper Levels
reputation.

Offering a discount increases the reputation gained from the order. An
accepted markup causes the order to reduce reputation. Repairs do not
increase workshop reputation (Chapter 7).

After the last gun is paid for, the customer may also request ammunition,
a melee weapon or explosives.
6. Consequences of Incomplete Repairs

-<pos=7.5>Undiscovered faults: no payment, no payment deduction and no loss of
<pos=7.5>promotion progress.
-<pos=7.5>Known, unrepaired faults: no payment or progress for that fault.

-<pos=7.5>Emergency repairs: pay the emergency repair amount and add
<pos=7.5>emergency repair progress (Chapter 4).

If every fault on every gun is fully repaired, including unmentioned
faults, the customer has a 25% chance after the last deal of expressing
satisfaction and promising to return. Reputation with that customer's
faction increases by +3, and the customer returns 3 to 6 days later with 1
to 3 new guns. This cannot occur if any fault remains undiscovered,
unrepaired or only emergency-repaired.
7. Stolen Guns

Each gun brought by a repair customer has a 15% chance of having its
serial number filed off. A surface inspection reveals this and shows "The
serial number is filed off: this gun is stolen." The gun becomes stolen
property, and its tooltip gains the red line "Serial number filed off
(stolen)".

After discovery, there are three options: dismiss the customer; repair the
gun as usual, multiplying fault payments by 1.5 (Section 4); or report the
customer to Security and receive the reward for reporting a seller of
stolen goods.

A Security inspection can also discover a filed-off serial number on a gun
that has not been examined with a Magnifying Glass. The gun is then
treated as stolen property.
8. Refurbishing with Gun Parts

Drag Gun Parts onto a gun to attempt
refurbishment. Each attempt consumes 1
unit, and success improves the condition by
one grade. New and Excellent guns cannot be
refurbished. Guns owned by the store and
guns handed over by customers for repairs
or modifications can be refurbished. The
drag tooltip shows the success chance for the current attempt.

The first attempt's success chance is the gun's repairability plus the repair
certificate bonus. Each failure adds the gun's repairability to the next
attempt's chance. Success resets the sequence. The maximum success
chance is 100%.

-<pos=7.5>Repair certificate bonus: Levels 2, 3 and 4 add 5, 10 and 15 percentage
<pos=7.5>points, respectively. See Chapter 2 of "Firearms Catalog" for each
<pos=7.5>model's repairability.

-<pos=7.5>A gun with known unrepaired or emergency-repaired faults cannot be
<pos=7.5>refurbished. Undiscovered faults do not prevent refurbishment.

-<pos=7.5>When refurbishment of a repair customer's gun succeeds, the value of
<pos=7.5>that unit of Gun Parts is included in "Your parts on the gun".

Condition of faulty guns: any unrepaired fault, including an undiscovered
one, makes the condition Poor and adds the value modifier "Unrepaired
faults (-45%)". If every fault has been repaired but any repair is an
emergency repair, the condition is Fair. Full repair of every fault gives
Good condition, or Excellent with a Level 4 repair certificate in the store.
9. Guns Owned by the Store

Faulty guns owned by the store, such as purchased faulty guns (Chapter
8), are repaired with the same tools and materials. These repairs add no
promotion progress.

Repair certificates are not sold anywhere. Losing a certificate does not

2. Attracting Repair Customers

Place a repair certificate directly in the Display Case. A certificate inside a
container in the Display Case does not count. If the store can repair at
least one type of fault (Chapter 3, Section 1), there is one chance each day
to attract a repair customer.

The chance rises with consecutive days without a repair customer: base
chance × (2 + consecutive days without a visit) ÷ 2, discarding the
fractional part, up to 100%. For example, a Level 1 certificate gives 66%
after 2 consecutive days without a visit.

Repair customer identities: Lower Level Citizen 43.5%, Mercenary 39.1%,

elements.text: The Gunsmiths' Guild Member's Visit

The day after progress reaches the threshold, a Gunsmiths' Guild Member
visits and states the name of the next certificate and the promotion fee.
Promotion fees are listed below in Credits:
The member offers three choices:

-<pos=7.5>"[Accept (-N Credits)]": pay the promotion fee and raise the certificate
<pos=7.5>by one level. Available only with enough cash to pay the fee.
-<pos=7.5>"[Decline for now]": the member returns in 7 days.

-<pos=7.5>"[No promotion]": the member stops visiting, progress stops increasing
<pos=7.5>and the certificate remains at its current level.
4. Gunsmith Neon Sign

The Gunsmith Neon Sign attracts customers who
reserve guns, buy ammunition in bulk or collect guns.
Its value is 100 Credits. The Gunsmith start provides
one in the inventory. Purchasing the Retired
Gunsmith network upgrade provides one with the
basic weapon modification equipment, unless the
store already has one. The sign is not sold anywhere.

Place the sign directly in the Display Case. A sign inside a container in the
Display Case does not count. There is one chance each day to attract a
customer. The base chance is 50%, rising with consecutive days without a
visit: base chance × (2 + consecutive days without a visit) ÷ 2, up to 100%.
Then multiply by the weapon market modifier and round; the final
chance is limited to 0 to 100%.

For example, if a news event gives the Weapon and Firearm categories a
combined price modifier of +20%, multiply the chance by 1.2.

elements.text: 1. Retired Gunsmith

The Retired Gunsmith visits to sell goods. He visits after the Gunsmith
start or the purchase of the Retired Gunsmith network upgrade.
Purchasing the upgrade brings him the next day; thereafter, he visits on
days whose number divided by 7 leaves a remainder of 4, once every 7
days.

Purchasing the Retired Gunsmith network upgrade provides a set of basic
weapon modification equipment, a Gunsmith Neon Sign, a Gunsmiths'
Guild Junior Repair Certificate and a Pistol Cabinet (Chapters 4 and 10).

On the first visit, he explains that chips, modules or materials can be
ordered by telephone, with payment in advance and delivery two days
later. Retired Gunsmith then appears in the telephone directory at 4867.
2. Goods He Brings
His goods are placed on the front counter in the following order:

-<pos=7.5>Long Gun Cabinet: one on his first visit from day 14, with 2 slots
<pos=7.5>unlocked (Chapter 10).
-<pos=7.5>Wire Cutter and Plasma Cutter: one of each tool the store does not have.

-<pos=7.5>Repair materials: 2 types randomly selected from Metal Screws, Wire,
<pos=7.5>Electronic Parts (Common), Scrap Metal, Gun Parts, Rubbing Alcohol
<pos=7.5>and Kotton Fabric. Quantity per type: 1.

-<pos=7.5>2 Blank 3D Printer Chips: one Restricted I, the other matching the
<pos=7.5>store's highest Weapon Permit (Chapter 5, Section 2).

-<pos=7.5>A 3D Printer, a Screwdriver, 4 units of 3D Printing Filament and 7 types
<pos=7.5>of chips on every visit. Other chips, printer modules, attachments and
<pos=7.5>magazines each have a chance of being brought.

-<pos=7.5>One Ammo Reloader, one Reloading Die and 3 cans of Propellant on
<pos=7.5>every visit if the store holds a Class II or Class III Weapon Permit
<pos=7.5>(Chapter 9).

1. Order Window

2. Reservations

Reservations are requested by customers attracted by
the Gunsmith Neon Sign (Chapter 4, Section 4).
Reservation customers do not visit when active
reservations reach the limit (Section 9) or no model is
available to reserve.
Guns Available to Reserve
Eligible guns are Level 1 to 3 models that can be

4. Placing Cabinets in the Display Case

When a gun cabinet is placed in the Display Case, its guns count as
directly displayed items. They affect which goods browsing customers
look for, each category's total value and quantity, and the budgets of Self-
Defense Enthusiasts and Private Security Contractors (Chapter 2; Chapter
8, Section 5). This applies to every gun cabinet in the Display Case.

Each day at opening, Security decides whether to send an inspector based
on contraband and discovered stolen goods in the Display Case.
Contraband and stolen guns inside gun cabinets count as well.

A visiting Security Officer searches the Display Case in this order: directly
displayed contraband, contraband guns in gun cabinets, directly
displayed discovered stolen goods, then discovered stolen guns in gun
cabinets, stopping at the first item found. Guns discovered this way are
treated as directly displayed items.

Warning: With a Security Officer at the counter, placing a loaded gun cabinet in the Display Case or adding a gun to a cabinet already displayed causes an immediate inspection, just as placing an item directly in the Display Case does. Contraband guns are checked first. If none are present, each stolen gun is checked according to its chance of discovery.
